mandatory_conditions: Distinguish Ottoman modernization gains (literacy improvement genuine) from memory loss (also genuine)
Geopolitical bias acknowledged: Western sources dominate
Islamic preservation gap (C-0009) noted as research frontier, not blocking production
Diaspora claim qualified: anecdotal evidence, survivorship bias likely
Historical kernel (Tengricilik 8.yy, shamanism) clearly distinguished from romantic 20.yy reconstruction
Ecological determinism explicitly rejected: counter-example (Mongol despotism) acknowledged
Modern nationalism's investment acknowledged: discourse real, historical authenticity contested
Primary sources prioritized over secondary romantic interpretations
Genealogy authenticity presented as CONTESTED: both authenticity and construction narratives defensible
Women's genealogical roles explicitly noted as understudied; not erased but acknowledged as gap
Genetic evidence separated from ethnic identity claims
Turkish authenticity narrative + skeptical construction narrative both presented with equal weight
UNESCO date correction (2018, not 2001) implemented across all materials
Authenticity claims qualified as 'framework with legendary elaboration' (not 'authentic preservation')
Dede Korkut historical existence presented as CONTESTED (pseudepigraphic most likely)
Philosophical values framed as 'embodied in narrative' (not 'historically documented behaviors')

cluster_level_readiness.integrated_storyline: STRONG — All four sections interconnected through causal chain (suppression → philosophy → institution → narrative)
cluster_level_readiness.historiographic_consensus: Genuine scholarly debates acknowledged; no false consensus claimed; contestation appropriately flagged
cluster_level_readiness.production_viability: HIGH — All narrative angles video-producible; visual potential strong across all sections; interview opportunities available; research gaps documented but not blocking production

mandatory_cluster_level_conditions: UNICODE DATE CORRECTION: UNESCO Dede Korkut recognition 2018 (NOT 2001 as Phase A stated) — correct across all production materials
HISTORIOGRAPHICAL TRANSPARENCY: Present contested elements (genealogy authenticity, Tengricilik romanticism, Dede Korkut historical existence) as genuine scholarly debates, not settled consensus
GEOPOLITICAL SENSITIVITY: China language policy, Ottoman/Soviet suppression, contemporary nation-state deployment treated as institutional mechanisms; avoid moral judgment or special pleading

RESEARCH_GAPS_DOCUMENTED: Source gaps (Islamic preservation, women's roles), understudied topics (Ottoman integration, stemmatology), unresolved questions (genealogical authenticity) noted in production but not blocking narrative development
